Recombinase discovery in Xanthobacter — results explorer

A read-only companion to recombinase_workflow.py. That notebook needs BLAST+, HMMER, MAFFT, skani, the NCBI datasets CLI and ~5 GB of genome FASTA to produce these numbers; this one needs nothing but the tables it ships with (≈120 kB), so it runs anywhere: locally, on molab, in the browser via WebAssembly, or as a static page. What is here: Pfam/PSI-BLAST hit tables, the deduplicated bench shortlist, SSAP↔exonuclease operon calls, ANI and pairwise-identity matrices, and the reference-phage cross-references. Every table carries its provenance (source file + SHA-256) in the Data provenance tab. To regenerate the bundle after re-running the workflow: 
cd Recombinase_Search
python share/build_bundle.py      # writes share/data/*.csv + manifest.json
Loaded 15 tables from the xanthobacter_121 bundle (126 kB).

Deduplicated groups of recombinases. ngens is how many genomes carry the group; redundant are near-identical variants (≥90% id) and distinct are the 70–90% members worth testing separately.
SSAP = single-strand annealing protein (RecT / ERF / Rad52); EXO = the exonuclease it must be paired with for dsDNA recombination. relation says whether the pair shares a strand — same-strand pairs are the cleaner operon candidates.
Every table below is a normalized copy of a workflow artifact (see source). Empty or stale artifacts are excluded; the workflow's absolute local paths are stripped. Full hashes are in share/data/manifest.json.

data.text/markdown:
Reproducing this

The numbers here come from recombinase_workflow.py, which needs blast+, hmmer, mafft, skani/fastani and the NCBI datasets CLI plus the 121-genome input set. That environment is not available in a browser, which is exactly why this notebook only reads the distilled tables. 
cd Recombinase_Search
marimo edit recombinase_workflow.py      # the search (needs the CLIs)
python share/build_bundle.py             # distill results -> share/data/
marimo edit recombinase_results_explorer.py
  • Source notebook: recombinase_workflow.py
  • Bundle manifest: share/data/manifest.json
  • Repository: nakrasian/recombineering
When reusing these results, cite the bundle commit — the SHA-256 in the provenance tab pins the exact tables.
